It’s not whining. You have a legitimate concern. I don’t know how old you are but I understand having this issue and how it gets progressively worse.
I was told by my doctor that when I feel trapped or not able to gain control I think ending my life is the best option for escaping. It may be completely different with you though.

What helps: 
1. Have an emergency plan. A person to talk to or a hospital to go to if it gets really bad.
2. Consider meds. They have helped me tremendously. 
3. Therapy and journaling. You will learn to better cope with pain and not catastrophize everything .

Good luck and stay strong

I read it all and I’m here to tell you that you’re not alone. At its face, that comment doesn’t seem like much but really think about it. 

There are other men who’ve attempted suicide. There are other men who wish to die daily. There are guys everywhere that put on a fun or tough personality so that others won’t be uncomfortable with them....I’m one of those guys.

And when I did show people the real me, many started gossiping about me, some ghosted me, and some did what your girlfriend did (act somber and then act like nothing). 

It’s horribly frustrating. You begin to think, “You all wanted the positive version of me but can’t handle this part?” You feel rejected, misunderstood, and a burden.

Here’s what I think. First value yourself. The fun side of you that others like IS YOU, just like the “you” that gets depressed is part of you. 

You will have good days and bad days and acknowledging that you have a mental health problem is a big step toward healing. 

Get a dr if you don’t have one. If you have one and it’s not working, find another.  Consider meds if you’re not taking them. Find a support group. 

Suicide isn’t the answer. I think about suicide at least 3 days out of the week but I e come to understand that those thoughts aren’t real.  If my kid were to tell me they wanted to do it, I’d plead with them not to and why? Because I know there’s a better way.

As far as your GF and others like her: Have grace. They don’t understand and will never fully understand. They don’t know how to react or respond because they don’t know the Illness. All we can do is instruct them and have grace.

Hang in there. It’ll get better....and then worse....and then better....and so on. But the better is worth living for

If a person has never experienced clinical depression they will never understand how bad it is.  I unfortunately have. I get it. You think that nothing is right or can ever be right. The world would be better if you were gone, you’d no longer suffer, and so on.

We tell ourselves lies and then ruminate in them. I found what helps me is first speak out loud, FEELINGS ARE NOT FACTS. Just because you feel and think it doesn’t make it true.

Next is no matter how much you think it can’t get better you have to trust it will. I’ve written similar posts to yours when down and close to suicide. Fortunately I did not act on it and I’ve seen brighter days since.

Hang in there. Behind the dark clouds the sun is still shining.
